note: Positions at epoch 2026.0. Proper motions in mas/yr; pmSource says where each comes from.

targets.name: Barnard's Star
targets.blurb: The star with the fastest motion across our sky: about 10 arcseconds a year, northwards.

targets.name: WISE 0855−0714
targets.blurb: The coldest known brown dwarf, 7.4 light years away, moving about 8 arcseconds a year. Dark in visible light; it glows only at the longest SPHEREx wavelengths.

spotFact.text: Very faint below about 4 µm and bright near 4.5 µm, so in SPHEREx's shorter colours a blend with a nearby star is mostly the star.
sources: Schneider et al. 2016, ApJ 823, L35 (HST F125W, F160W); arXiv:1605.05618
spotFact.checked: 2026-11-15, by the event build; Physics' memory value J ≈ 25 was Faherty et al. 2014's tentative 2.6σ ground-based value

centreShift.what: Light centre (app's recentre: brightest pixel within 1 px, then 3x3 flux-weighted centroid) in each per-detector stack, started from the all-colour later look's recentred spot; distances to Gaia DR3 5756956644387831296 (G 16.3, BP-RP 0.72) and to WISE 0855's predicted place, each moved to the look's mean date.
centreShift.measured: 2026-11-15, event build; fixed before writing any text (Physics' rule: write the clause only if the centre moves by more than ~2 arcsec)
centreShift.caveat: A 3x3 centroid pulls towards the peak pixel and pixel phase adds error, so these are rough; the shift is clear (more than 2 arcsec in every D5/D6 stack).
centreShift.onTheLine: Physics, 15 Nov: in all four D5/D6 cases the two distances add up to the separation (9.6 vs 9.5; 6.4 vs 6.4), so the centres lie on the line between the sources, as a two-source blend does. Fractions along the line (~40-65%) are information only: a 3x3 centroid is biased towards the peak pixel. Centroid error at S/N 9-14 is about 1 arcsec.

targets.name: Epsilon Indi B
targets.blurb: A pair of brown dwarfs orbiting the star Epsilon Indi, 12 light years away, moving about 4.7 arcseconds a year.
targets.pmSource: Gaia DR3 (Epsilon Indi A, shared motion)

targets.name: RW Aurigae
targets.blurb: A young star still wrapped in dust, whose brightness changes as clouds pass in front of it.
targets.blendNote: RW Aurigae A and B are about 1.4 arcsec apart, inside one SPHEREx pixel, so the ratio is their combined light

targets.name: R Draconis
targets.blurb: A pulsating red giant (a Mira variable) that brightens and fades over about 245 days.
